data.name: Nayantak
data.gender_notes: Nayantak is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from Sanskrit, Nayana meaning 'eyes' and Tak meaning 'takes'. The name Nayantak carries the meaning “One who takes the eyes” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nayantak usually hope their child will grow to embody one who takes the eyes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power to perceive and understand the world.
data.etymology: Nayantak belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who takes the eyes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nayantak total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Nayantak" carries deep cultural significance in Hinduism, where eyes are considered the windows to the soul. It emphasizes the importance of perception and observation, emphasizing qualities such as beauty, truth, and wisdom.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Nayantak" can be understood through its connection to the god Shiva, who is commonly referred to as "Nayana Taraka," or the one who liberates the soul from the cycle of birth and death through His divine gaze. It is believed that One who possesses this name is bestowed with Shiva's divine vision and spiritual insight.

It is a reminder of the inherent strength within each one of us to overcome obstacles and achieve our goals.
